Document: Hospital Saint Joseph Hospital of Valmontone Doctor Francesca Perri , Internal Medicine Specialist Patient Carla Ferrara  The patient, a 35-year-old woman, comes to the consultation due to a series of symptoms that require detailed medical evaluation.   The patient reports the presence of an epidermoid cyst in the armpit, as well as the observation of a dotted pattern on the epiphysis of the distal phalanx of the third finger of the hand. In addition, a streak on the ovary and an enlargement of the vestibule of the inner ear have been identified. Simple cortical cysts, atrophy of the pectoral muscle and lethal dysplasia with short limbs have been detected. Likewise, the patient has been diagnosed with proximal tubule disease.  Tests performed Imaging studies have been performed to evaluate the presence of the cysts and the bone alterations mentioned. In addition, blood tests and genetic tests have been carried out to confirm the diagnosis of lethal dysplasia with short limbs.   The recommended treatment includes specialized follow-up by a multidisciplinary team, with the aim of comprehensively addressing the different clinical manifestations present in the patient.  Conclusions A personalized follow-up and treatment plan has been established for the patient, in order to monitor the evolution of the various conditions identified.

Hospital Holy Cross Hospital Doctor Elena Marini Specialist in Internal Medicine Patient Emanuele Rossi   The patient, 30 years old, comes to the consultation due to a series of symptoms that have worried him in recent weeks. The main symptoms include the presence of a flat head, crossed kidney with fusion, accumulation of pigment in the trabecular meshwork, dysfunction of the mental muscle, recessive inheritance linked to the X chromosome and premature ejaculation.    The patient has no relevant medical history in his clinical history.    On performing the physical examination, it is observed that the patient has an abnormal head shape, with the presence of a crossed kidney with fusion when performing abdominal palpation. In addition, there is evidence of accumulation of pigment in the ocular trabecular meshwork, as well as dysfunction of the mental muscle. The possible recessive inheritance linked to the X chromosome must be taken into account in this case.    Additional studies will be carried out to confirm the diagnosis, taking into account the clinical characteristics present in the patient.    Once the results of the studies are obtained, a personalized treatment plan will be established to address each of the symptoms present in the patient.  The patient is given an appointment for follow-up and control of his/her health status.

Hospital Sun Queen Hospital Doctor Elena Colombo Endocrinology Specialist Patient Giovanni Rizzo  The patient, 45 years old, comes to the consultation due to a series of symptoms that have been appearing progressively in recent months. Among the most relevant symptoms are asymmetric sclerosis of the phalanx of the right hand finger, swelling in the ankles, unjustified excessive growth, pancreatic inflammation, delayed mineralization of the trapezoid bone, external nasal malformation, presence of renal cortical and medullary cysts, as well as sclerosis of the metaphysis.   On examination, the presence of deformities in the phalanges of the right hand, edema in the ankles, acromegaly with coarse facial features, and evident external nasal malformation are observed. In addition, renal cysts are palpated on abdominal palpation.   After carrying out complementary tests such as X-rays, MRI and blood tests, the diagnosis of Albright Syndrome is reached, a rare genetic disease that affects calcium metabolism and is characterized by the presence of various skeletal and endocrine abnormalities.   The treatment will be based on the control of calcium levels in the blood, the management of renal and pancreatic complications, as well as multidisciplinary follow-up with endocrinology, nephrology and surgery in necessary cases.  A check-up is scheduled in one month for follow-up and evaluation of response to treatment.

Hospital Molinetti Hospital of Rivoli Doctor Paolo Galli Specialist in Internal Medicine Patient Marta Romano  The patient, aged 45, comes to the consultation due to a sudden increase in blood ammonia, uneven sclerosis of the middle phalanx of the finger, wedge-shaped big toe, nephrogenic remains around the lobes, optic nerve fissure, hyposecretion of hypothalamic LH-releasing hormone, tendency to act without thinking, and parathyroid hyperplasia.   The patient has no relevant medical history.   Uneven sclerosis of the middle phalanx of the right hand finger and wedge-shaped big toe is observed. Likewise, an optic nerve fissure is evident in the ophthalmological examination.  Complementary studies Blood tests were performed, which revealed a significant increase in ammonia levels, as well as nephrogenic remains around the lobes. In addition, hyposecretion of hypothalamic LH-releasing hormone was found in hormonal tests. Ultrasound showed parathyroid hyperplasia.   After evaluating the symptoms and the results of complementary studies, the diagnosis of Reye's syndrome was established, a rare disease that mainly affects the liver and brain.   Treatment with medications will be started to control blood ammonia levels, as well as follow-up with specialists for the management of parathyroid hyperplasia.  The patient is scheduled for a check-up in one month.

Hospital Molinetti Hospital of Rivoli Doctor Francesco Leone Hematology Specialist Patient Pietro Messina  The patient, 55 years old, comes to the doctor's office because of nonspecific symptoms such as fatigue, involuntary weight loss, palpitations, and excessive sweating. In addition, he reports constant headache and blurred vision.   The patient has a history of high blood pressure and smoking.   Pale skin-mucosal color and tachycardia at rest are observed. Hospital Saint Felix Hospital Doctor Carla Fontana Medical Specialist in Genetics Patient Ilaria Bianchi  The patient, 25 years old, comes to the consultation presenting a complex clinical picture. She reports respiratory failure, respiratory ciliary dysfunction, fluid accumulation under the retina, sodium regulation disorder, congenital neutropenia, and a history of recurrent Neisseria meningitidis infections.   The patient shows signs of respiratory difficulty, presence of edema in the retina, hyponatremia, and neutropenia.  Complementary studies Laboratory studies were performed that revealed an increase in copper bound to non-ceruloplasmin in the blood.   In the presence of the symptoms and the results of the studies, the diagnosis of Menkes Syndrome is established, a rare genetic disease characterized by dysfunction of copper transport in the body.   Treatment with copper supplements will be started and follow-up will be scheduled with the Genetics service for genetic counseling and comprehensive management of the disease.

Hospital Cardarelli Hospital of Montesilvano Doctor Daniele Vitale Specialist in Internal Medicine Patient Fabio Parisi  The patient, aged 55, comes to the consultation due to a postauricular cutaneous fistula, mixed dyslipidemia, cardiac tumor, sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome, abdominal aortic stenosis, vertebral osteophytes and a ureteral blockage.   The patient has a history of high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes and obesity.   The presence of a postauricular cutaneous fistula with purulent discharge is observed. In addition, the presence of vertebral osteophytes is evident on the spinal X-ray.  Complementary studies Blood tests were performed that confirmed the presence of mixed dyslipidemia. Echocardiography revealed the presence of a cardiac tumor. Polysomnography showed a high rate of apneas and hypopneas per hour, consistent with sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome. Abdominal ultrasound revealed abdominal aortic stenosis. Finally, CT showed ureteral obstruction.   1. Postauricular cutaneous fistula 2. Mixed dyslipidemia 3. Cardiac tumor 4. Sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome 5. Abdominal aortic stenosis 6. Vertebral osteophytes 7. Ureteral obstruction   Antibiotic treatment is indicated for the cutaneous fistula, statins for dyslipidemia, evaluation by the cardiology department for the cardiac tumor, CPAP for the sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome, evaluation by vascular surgery for the abdominal aortic stenosis, physical therapy for the vertebral osteophytes, and placement of a ureteral catheter for the ureteral obstruction.  A follow-up appointment is scheduled in one month to monitor the prescribed treatments.
